markdown_report:
The best initial direction is a padding-aware temporal diagnostic adapter for the supplied NextItNet models. No measured diagnosis currently establishes stale-history interference; user feedback motivates testing that hypothesis. The adapter supports subsequent improvements rather than directly improving ranking.

Three starting insights guide the design. (1) Feedback favors specific recent connections. Interaction order can test model dependence, but cannot establish immediate purchase intent. (2) Existing margins describe sampled training separation. Score scaling can enlarge margins without changing rankings, so pairwise accuracy and fixed-candidate ranking measurements are also needed. (3) Left padding makes representation selection consequential. A count−1 readout can invalidate subsequent interpretations; use the largest nonzero index.

Three literature insights refine the proposal. (1) NextItNet’s causal convolutions impose a finite receptive field [1], potentially with unreachable offsets. Compaction changes lags, while biases and normalization can introduce padding effects. (2) Recency and order warrant separate interventions [2]. Deletion alone cannot distinguish stale content from changed geometry. (3) Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with catalog ranking [3]. Pinned validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion; unlabeled catalog statistics describe behavior only.

The resulting framework organizes three research directions:

| Direction | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Structural validity | Causality, exact reachable offsets, final-position readout, leading-padding consistency | Detect implementation faults before behavioral analysis |
| Temporal dependence | Prefix/suffix deletion, matched deletions, fixed-position replacements, recent/old order shuffling | Separate content, lag, boundary, and order effects; do not infer intent |
| Ranking discrimination | Fixed-pair accuracy, margins, norms, representation spectra, authorized fixed-candidate validation changes | Separate scaling, dimensional restriction, training separation, and benchmark performance |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Padding-aware temporal adapter: 5/7/5.** Originality: integrates established checks, but introduces no new backbone. Potential: supports auditable decisions, but perturbations can create unfamiliar inputs. Difficulty: existing hooks help, but geometry controls and user-level aggregation add work [1,2].
2. **Uniform-to-moderate negative curriculum: 4/7/5.** Originality: adapts established sampling, but resembles prior curricula. Potential: may improve discrimination, but unobserved items can be false negatives. Difficulty: preserves NextItNet, but adds sampling and training expense [4].
3. **Text-supported contrast probes: 6/6/6.** Originality: connects feedback to auditable contrasts, but uses familiar lexical methods. Potential: exposes broad-versus-specific rankings, but cannot establish compatibility. Difficulty: needs no external data, but requires attribute extraction and abstention.

At 0% progress, choose idea 1. Retain all diagnostic entry points. Predeclare strengths, seeds, length bins and eligibility; aggregate repeated measurements within users before category means and equal-weight macro averaging. Report definitions, counts and unavailable values as null. Require fixed-geometry corroboration before attributing deletion gains to stale content. Use pointwise paired user-bootstrap intervals; keep adaptive findings exploratory. Test geometry and causality first; restore model mode afterward. Mean cosine indicates alignment, not collapse: add variance, covariance effective rank and norm summaries [5,6].

Keep one checkpoint per category, unchanged routing, seeds, splits and selection. No diagnostic scores enter prediction. Later training changes require measured support and matching predictor definitions. Validation reuse risks search overfitting; uncertainty intervals do not remove it.

References: [1] [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py); [2] [recency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722); [3] [sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/); [4] [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf); [5] [anisotropy](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00512); [6] [RankMe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02885).

idea.description: Implement a padding-aware temporal diagnostic adapter around each existing NextItNet category model, combining structural checks, geometry-controlled history perturbations, scale-invariant pairwise accuracy, sampled margins, and representation statistics. Retain the existing single-model architecture and prediction behavior.
idea.motivation: Feedback suggests broad relevance and stale interests may displace specific recent matches, but existing measurements cannot establish either mechanism. Correct readout, padding behavior, receptive-field reach, and controlled comparisons are prerequisites for interpreting temporal sensitivity. Score scaling and anisotropy also require explicit controls before interpreting margins or embedding alignment as model quality.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all host ModelView interfaces. Use view.model as the actual trained network; preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Do not use unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores or simulator traits. Category breakdowns remain unavailable, not empty evidence of no failures. Use only public training histories and available titles/descriptions/timestamps.

Run under eval and no_grad, restoring the original training flag in finally. Use a local RNG seeded 42 without modifying global training RNG state. Select the largest nonzero sequence index and skip all-padding rows; endpoint supervised comparisons also require nonzero positive and negative IDs. Preserve identical target pairs across interventions. Baseline margins may use every valid supervised position, but label them position-weighted training statistics rather than user-level generalization estimates. Report P(s_positive > s_negative) + 0.5 P(tie), raw margin summaries, score distributions, embedding norms and feature norms. Fixed-pair accuracy is invariant to strictly increasing score transformations but remains conditional on sampled negative difficulty. Preserve the original mean-margin, tenth-percentile, below-zero and below-0.5 statistics; identify the 0.5 threshold as scale dependent.

Exclude padding/reserved tokens when sampling up to 2,048 real-item embeddings using seed 42. Rename the original cosine-derived collapse measurement as angular alignment, retaining its definition and explaining that approximately 0.5 means zero average cosine. For item embeddings and intact final history features separately, calculate centered covariance eigenvalues, total variance, leading-eigenvalue share and effective rank exp(-sum(p*log(p))), where p is normalized covariance eigenvalue mass. Report raw and unit-normalized spectra and norm quantiles. Treat zero total variance explicitly: report zero variance and null effective rank with a reason. This covariance statistic differs from RankMe's singular-value normalization. Neither high rank nor anisotropy establishes useful ranking.

Derive receptive-field span and exact reachable endpoint offsets from the actual convolution graph, including every temporal convolution and residual path. For stride-one chains, the span is 1 + sum((kernel_size-1)*dilation), but span alone does not establish offset reachability. Inspect normalization axes, biases, padding and intermediate masking; temporal normalization or global operations invalidate purely convolutional locality assumptions. Do not silently modify masking or normalization in a diagnostic-only change. Test future-token causality at intermediate valid positions, replacements outside reachable offsets where applicable, batch reordering, identical-input reruns, and supported leading-padding widths. Record actual input width, retained history and endpoint-relative lags; use numerical tolerance atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5 and report maximum absolute differences. Mark unsupported variable-width checks unavailable.

Predeclare temporal strengths as fractions 0.25 and 0.5 of original nonpadding length, with k=max(1,floor(fraction*length)); require enough remaining history for each intervention. Compare old-prefix and recent-suffix deletion with equal-count seeded random/interior deletions. For old/interior controls, preserve the newest k items; declare rows ineligible if the requested deletion cannot preserve them. Compare compacted deletions with zero replacement at the same positions, noting that interior zeros are an out-of-distribution diagnostic input. Add nonzero fixed-position old-item replacements drawn only from training-observed item IDs, excluding original IDs and the scored target pair, matched by training-frequency decile when available. Record unmatched replacements and avoid claiming semantic matching. Shuffle the recent k items and, separately, the old prefix while preserving item identities, multiplicities, positions and padding. Require at least two distinct items in the shuffled region. Use 20 seeded shuffle draws per eligible user and an identity control. Report intervention sizes, fixed-pair score/margin changes and eligibility counts. Treat compaction, zero replacement and alternative-item replacement as complementary controls, each with its own distribution-shift limitation.

The loader's four-tuple contains no user IDs, so do not infer independent users from rows or bootstrap positions. Use up to ten loader batches for descriptive training-position measurements. For user-level probes, construct intact left-padded sequences directly from user_train['History'], using the baseline's item mapping and maximum length. Freeze one sequence per available training user, or a deterministic seed-42 cap of 200 users/category if compute requires it. Without held-out targets, compare scores on a fixed seed-42 sample of 99 unseen real-item IDs/user; call these score-sensitivity measurements, not relevance, HR or target-rank estimates. If authorized validation access supplies user IDs, targets and pinned candidates, run validation interventions separately without changing the evaluator or candidate construction. Otherwise omit validation intervention metrics explicitly.

Average repeated intervention draws and any positions within each identified user, then calculate category means and their equal-weight macro average. Define length strata from original lengths as 1-10, 11-25 and 26+; report the baseline truncation length and every stratum's eligible count. Compare methods on common eligible users, and mark impossible/unchanged interventions ineligible rather than zero-effect. Cache only within this trial. Obtain pointwise 95% percentile intervals from 2,000 seed-42 bootstrap resamples of identified users within category, carrying each user's complete paired vector together. Report a four-category macro estimate only when all four categories have eligible observations. Intervals condition on fitted models, users and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed, candidate-sampling and adaptive-search uncertainty. This initial adapter is exploratory and does not manufacture p-values from bootstrap intervals. Any later confirmatory tests need a prespecified valid null procedure and Holm correction across the declared family; paired swaps require defensible exchangeability.

No diagnostic perturbation, score adjustment or independently fitted component enters production inference. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], four-category routing, one checkpoint/category, single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. Account for diagnostic GPU time within the shared 43,200-second budget. Future training proposals, including negative curricula, need validation evidence and checkpoint/predictor-writer consistency. Do not read other trials or hidden test data.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        previous_mode = view.model.training
        rng = local_rng(seed=42)
        measurements, definitions = initialize_declared_schema()
        try:
            view.model.eval()
            with no_grad():
                inspect_actual_convolutions_normalization_padding_and_masks()
                derive_span_and_reachable_offsets_or_record_unavailable()
                sample_real_item_embeddings(max_items=2048, rng=rng)
                collect_alignment_norms_raw_and_normalized_covariance_statistics()

                for batch in first_at_most_ten_batches(train_loader):
                    _, sequence, positive, negative = batch
                    features = view.log2feats(sequence)
                    logits = view.predict_score(features, stack(positive, negative, dim=-1))
                    valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0) & (negative != 0)
                    collect_position_weighted_margins_accuracy_scores_and_counts(logits, valid)
                    collect_endpoint_features_at_largest_nonzero_indices(features, sequence)
                    run_supported_identity_batch_causality_and_padding_checks()
                    for eligible row with a valid supervised endpoint:
                        pair = fixed_positive_negative_ids_at_endpoint(row)
                        for declared temporal intervention and matched control:
                            altered, eligibility, geometry = transform(row, rng)
                            if eligible and changed:
                                score_same_pair_at_largest_nonzero_index(altered, pair)
                                collect_descriptive_paired_margin_change_and_geometry()

                identified_users = deterministic_users_from_public_training_histories(cap=200, seed=42)
                for user in identified_users:
                    intact = baseline_encode_and_left_pad(user.history)
                    candidates = fixed_training_only_unseen_sample(user, size=99, rng=rng)
                    skip_with_reason_if_no_eligible_candidates_or_history()
                    baseline_scores = score_at_largest_nonzero_index(intact, candidates)
                    for strength in [0.25, 0.5]:
                        build_deletions_matched_controls_zero_and_nonzero_replacements()
                        build_20_recent_and_old_region_shuffles_plus_identity()
                        for eligible changed intervention:
                            score_identical_candidates_at_correct_endpoint()
                            record_paired_score_sensitivity_and_intervention_metadata()
                    average_repeated_draws_within_user()

                if authorized_validation_interface_available:
                    evaluate_paired_interventions_on_unchanged_pinned_users_targets_candidates()
                else:
                    record_validation_interventions_as_unavailable()
        finally:
            view.model.train(previous_mode)

        summarize_training_position_metrics_separately_from_user_metrics()
        aggregate_common_eligible_users_by_category_and_original_length_bin()
        macro_average_only_when_all_four_categories_are_available()
        bootstrap_identified_users_within_category(draws=2000, seed=42)
        return {'metrics': summarize_or_null_with_counts_and_reasons(),
                'metric_definitions': definitions}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    serialize(raw_diagnosis['metrics'], raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'])
    request_evidence_linked_findings_with_counts_controls_uncertainty_and_missingness()
    prohibit_invented_measurements_intent_compatibility_or_feedback_conclusions()
    distinguish_training_separation_score_sensitivity_and_validation_ranking()
    require_geometry_control_corroboration_for_stale_content_hypotheses()
    label_adaptive_or_uncontrolled_findings_exploratory()

originality.positive: Combines NextItNet-specific structural validation, geometry-controlled temporal interventions and scale-aware diagnostics in a reproducible adapter.
originality.negative: The constituent methods are established; the contribution is integration rather than a novel learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can identify actionable implementation defects and distinguish temporal mechanisms before spending the search budget on retraining.
future_potential.negative: It does not directly improve HR@10, and controlled perturbations still cannot establish user intent or real-world utility.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing model hooks, training histories and small cached measurements without requiring another trained predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact receptive-field inspection, matched controls, missing user IDs in the loader, reproducible eligibility and paired aggregation make it more complex than the original rating suggested.

related_work.title: NextItNet and author implementation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for receptive-field, causality and endpoint checks.
The author implementation at https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py helps distinguish residual blocks with multiple temporal convolutions from bottleneck variants.
limitations: Architecture alone does not establish which interactions a fitted model uses.
The actual supplied modules must be inspected; theoretical span can contain unreachable offsets.
Does not validate this diagnostic adapter on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: NextItNet normalization, biases and padding implementation
contributions: Provides concrete implementation details motivating inspection of normalization axes, convolution biases and padding states.
Supports checking whether explicit leading padding behaves like implicit layer boundaries.
limitations: This implementation need not match the supplied PyTorch baseline.
Padding-invariance claims require verification of actual operation order and masks.

related_work.title: Study of excessive recency bias in sequential recommendation
contributions: Motivates measuring recency dependence rather than assuming stronger recency is always beneficial.
limitations: Does not establish excessive or insufficient recency dependence in the supplied checkpoints.
Deletion effects require controls for changed lags, receptive-field membership and boundaries.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and model comparisons.
limitations: Does not provide missing full-catalog relevance labels or justify changing the pinned evaluator.
Bootstrap precision does not eliminate sampled-to-catalog bias.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up and curriculum-based negative difficulty.
Identifies risks of premature hard-negative training and fixed hardest-item selection.
limitations: Does not establish that unobserved similar products are genuine negatives.
Benefits for the four-category NextItNet task require controlled validation.

related_work.title: Contextual embedding geometry and anisotropy
contributions: Motivates distinguishing average angular alignment from information loss.
limitations: Studies language representations rather than the supplied recommender.
Mean cosine alone cannot establish dimensional collapse or recommendation quality.

related_work.title: Dimensional collapse in representation learning
contributions: Motivates inspecting representation spectra rather than relying on mean cosine.
Supports separating dimensional restriction from nearly constant representations.
limitations: Spectral concentration does not by itself establish poor recommendation quality.
Uniformly small variance requires separate measurement from effective rank.

related_work.title: RankMe
contributions: Provides a spectral effective-rank approach for representation assessment.
Motivates explicit definitions when comparing rank statistics.
limitations: RankMe normalizes singular values; the proposed covariance effective rank normalizes covariance eigenvalues.
High effective rank can reflect noise and does not guarantee useful ranking.

related_work.title: Offline evaluation guidance
contributions: Provides general evaluation guidance relevant to fixed comparison protocols and clearly defined aggregation.
limitations: Does not establish the entire proposed NextItNet intervention protocol as a validated standard.
Predeclared controls cannot eliminate all perturbation distribution shift.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling, supporting preservation of each user's complete intervention vector.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified macro percentile bootstrap requires explicit implementation.
Intervals remain conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates and do not correct adaptive search.

related_work.title: SciPy permutation-test documentation
contributions: Documents permutation schemes and their assumptions for paired comparisons.
limitations: Paired label swaps require defensible exchangeability under the null.
Diagnostic history shuffles are interventions, not automatically inferential permutations.

related_work.title: Holm multiple-testing correction
contributions: Provides familywise-error correction under arbitrary dependence for a prespecified family of valid tests.
limitations: Cannot repair invalid individual tests, adaptive hypothesis selection or repeated validation tuning.
Does not turn pointwise bootstrap intervals into simultaneous intervals.
